seen_animation: Frames 1-5: a lion drawn in black lines lies along a ground line with its head on the right, facing right. The face is an oval with dot eyes and a smile, and jagged mane strokes sit above and behind the head. The body is a long low shape that ends in a pointed hind paw on the left. Grey clouds, a grey tree at the top right and grey grass tufts are in the scenery. Frames 6-8: the lion slides steadily to the right. By frame 8 its head is cut off by the right edge, and a few spikes of a second mane show at the left edge at head height. Frame 9: the second lion's head comes in at the left edge, facing the viewer with a round face and a ring of spikes. The first lion's back and hind paw are now on the right. A grey tree trunk comes into the scenery at the top left. Frame 10: the second head moves right and still faces the viewer, with no body visible. Frame 11: the second head has turned into a right-facing profile. The face oval has moved to the right of the mane, and the start of a body shows at the left edge. Frames 12-16: the second lion lies left of centre in profile facing right. Its head sits under the grey tree trunk, its body runs off the left edge, and the first lion's rear paw stays at the right edge. These frames change very little.
seen_film: Frames 1-4: a white male lion lies on a rock ledge with its head on the right, facing right, in front of dark foliage. Frames 5-8: the camera pans left, so the lion moves to the right in the frame. By frame 8 its head is cut off at the right edge, and a birch trunk and a pale shape come into view at the left. Frame 9: a second lion's head, facing the camera, is at the left edge, and the first lion's back is on the right. Frames 10-12: the second lion's head moves toward the left third of the frame and turns from facing the camera to a right-facing profile. Frames 13-16: the second lion lies in profile facing right, a little left of centre under the birch. The first lion's rump is at the right edge, and there is very little motion.
named_subject: A lion lying down (two lions seen in turn as the view pans: first one lion, then a second one)
evidence: Frames 1-4: the lion holds still in the same pose and place as in the film. Frames 5-8: it moves right at almost the same rate as the film's pan. The head sits at about 30%, 40% and 50% of the frame in frames 6, 7 and 8, and the head is cut off at the right edge in frame 8, as in the film. Frame 9: the second lion's head enters at the left edge facing the viewer while the first lion's back sits on the right, matching film frame 9. Frames 10-12: the second head moves right and turns to profile, matching film frames 10-12. Frames 13-16: the second lion settles in profile under the tree trunk with the first lion's rear at the right edge, matching film frames 13-16. The grey birch trunk appears from frame 7-9 onward, as the film's birch does. The first lion in frames 1-8 is drawn with the doodle's construction: a long low body, a pointed hind paw, a notch for the belly, an oval face with a smile, and jagged hair strokes over the head.
primary_gap: The second lion's head goes from a frontal sunburst (a round face inside a full ring of spikes) in frame 10 to a profile oval with the mane behind it in frame 11, with no in-between drawing. This change happens within one frame, so it can read as a swap. The second lion also keeps a full ring of spikes in frames 13-16, while the doodle's mane is a few jagged strokes over the top and back of the head.
closes_when: Frame 11 shows a three-quarter head, with the face oval only partly shifted toward the right and the spikes still partly on the right side, between the frontal head of frame 10 and the profile of frame 12. In frames 13-16 the second lion's mane is reduced to the doodle's few jagged strokes over the top and back of the head.
